digest.en: Honduras ex-President Hernandez is set to return home after receiving a Trump pardon, marking a significant shift in US-Honduras relations. Meanwhile, a deadly clash in the West Bank has led to Israeli settlers setting fire to mosques, sparking concerns over escalating tensions in the region.
digest.hi: होर्मुज स्ट्रेट में फिर बड़ा धमाका हुआ है, जिसमें एक तेल टैंकर समुद्री माइन से टकराया और उड़ गया। ईरानी मीडिया का दावा है कि जहाज नेवल माइन से टकराया था। इस घटना के बाद, अमेरिका के राष्ट्रपति ट्रंप से ईरान के मुद्दे पर बातचीत होने वाली है, जिसमें इजरायल के प्रधानमंत्री बेंजामिन नेतन्याहू भी शामिल होंगे।

articles.title: Honduras ex-President Hernandez to return home after Trump pardon
articles.summary: He is expected to appear ‌before a court on August 3 to face charges of fraud ‌and ⁠money laundering. An arrest warrant issued against him was suspended in ⁠June, meaning he will not be detained upon arrival Honduras ex-President Hernandez to return home after Trump pardon.

articles.title: Germany says fatal Berlin Pride attack believed to be an act of Islamic extremist terror
articles.summary: The suspect in Saturday night’s (July 25) attack remains at large. Authorities issued a wanted notice and warned people against approaching Abdul Ballout, a German citizen with Lebanese roots, saying that he may be armed and dangerous. Germany says fatal Berlin Pride attack believed to be an act of Islamic extremist terror.

articles.title: 10 killed after Typhoon Noul makes landfall in southern China
articles.summary: Noul, the 12th and the strongest typhoon to hit China so far this year, made landfall at Huizhou city in Guangdong around 3:50 a. m., bringing gale-force winds and heavy rain to large parts of the region 10 killed after Typhoon Noul makes landfall in southern China.

articles.title: Israeli settlers set fire to West Bank mosques after deadly clash
articles.summary: Four Palestinians and two Israeli ⁠soldiers. one of them acting as a local security coordinator. had been killed when a crowd of Israeli settlers made an incursion around the Palestinian village of Tal, southwest of Nablus Israeli settlers set fire to West Bank mosques after deadly clash.

articles.title: U.K. PM Burnham vows to put 'Britain's interest first' in Trump ties
articles.summary: I can't at any point say that I won't take a different opinion from him, that I will need to voice a different idea that is right for Britain. And I will do that, says U. K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham U. PM Burnham vows to put 'Britain's interest first' in Trump ties. U. U. K.

articles.title: Indian seafarer killed in attack on ship in Black Sea
articles.summary: The External Affairs Ministry said MV Omorfi was attacked while transiting the Black Sea, reportedly in Russian territorial waters; at the time of the incident, there were 10 crew members on board, including three Indians Indian seafarer killed in attack on ship in Black Sea.

articles.title: Nepal eases post-demonetisation curbs on Indian currency; allows ₹200, ₹500 notes
articles.summary: Following the demonetisation, Nepal prohibited the entry and use of Indian currency notes of denominations above ₹100; while the ceiling of ₹25,000 on carrying Indian currency remained unchanged, travellers were effectively restricted to notes of ₹100 and below. Nepal eases post-demonetisation curbs on Indian currency; allows ₹200, ₹500 notes.

articles.title: Venezuelan men sue aviation firms who flew them to notorious Salvadorian jail
articles.summary: Exclusive: CSI Aviation and GlobalX accused of violating civil rights as part of Trump immigration crackdownVenezuelan men sent last year to a notorious Salvadorian terrorism prison by the Trump administration are suing the US aviation companies that transported them there. Venezuela men sue aviation firms who flew them to notorious Salvadorian jail. Venezuelan men sue aviation firms who flew them to notorious Salvadorian jail.

articles.title: Street-smart youth take their declaration to the UN
articles.summary: When Samantha Richards and Angela Hifume walked into the Hall of Flags at United Nations Headquarters last week, they carried more than a folder of paper. They carried the voices of hundreds of street-connected children who had never expected anyone to listen. Street-smart youth take their declaration to the UN.

articles.title: UN chief hails Syria’s ‘moment of possibility’ on first visit since fall of Assad regime
articles.summary: Syria has an opportunity not only to recover from conflict but to build “a future that is more stable, more inclusive and more prosperous for all Syrians”, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said in Damascus on Saturday as he began a landmark visit to the country. UN chief hails Syria’s ‘moment of possibility’ on first visit since fall of Assad regime.

articles.title: Attacks On Chinese Projects Test China-Pakistan 'Iron Brotherhood' In Balochistan
articles.summary: China's investments in Pakistan's Balochistan are increasingly at risk as attacks by separatists are on the rise in the impoverished region. The worsening security situation has strained ties between the Iron Brothers, raising concerns over the future of Beijing's investments in Pakistan. Attacks On Chinese Projects Test China-Pakistan 'Iron Brotherhood' In Balochistan.

articles.summary: The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelensky, has dismissed the country’s commander-in-chief, Oleksandr Syrskyi, after a turbulent week in which he also removed his defense minister, Mykhailo Fedorov. The dismissal of the popular defense minister, who is credited by many as the brains behind Ukraine’s successful drone strategy, brought thousands onto the streets in protest. articles.summary: Today, Indonesia stands as one of the most formidable digital economic powerhouses in Southeast Asia. articles.title: Trump Says Iran 'Far More Serious' In Talks, Even As Attacks Intensify, Widen In Region
articles.summary: US President Donald ⁠Trump ⁠said Washington and Tehran were still conducting negotiations to end their conflict -- even as attacks intensified throughout the region, further threatening to widen the conflict into a full-blown Middle East war. Trump Says Iran 'Far More Serious' In Talks, Even As Attacks Intensify, Widen In Region.

articles.title: Iranian Sisters, 20, Tried In High-Profile Case Tied To January Protests
articles.summary: Sixteen people are facing charges connected to protests in Isfahan in January, during which a colonel in Iran's Revolutionary Guard was killed. Rights defenders are raising concerns about the legitimacy of the case, including the charges against 20-year-old sisters Taraneh and Romina Rahimi. Iranian Sisters, Aged 20, Tried In High-Profile Case Tied To January Protests. Iranian Sisters, 20, Tried In High-Profile Case Tied To January Protests.

articles.title: Russia's 'Axis Of Upheaval' Is Built To Last Beyond Ukraine, Analyst Kendall-Taylor Says
articles.summary: Russia's deepening partnerships with China, Iran, and North Korea represent one of the most significant geopolitical realignments driven by the war in Ukraine. Yet according to Andrea Kendall-Taylor, viewing this grouping through the lens of a traditional military alliance misses the bigger picture. Russia's 'Axis Of Upheaval' Is Built To Last Beyond Ukraine, Analyst Kendall-Taylor Says.

articles.title: Guyanese authorities confirm death of 72 people in sinking of coastal ferry
articles.summary: Guyanese authorities confirm 72 deaths after a state ferry capsized off the coast, leaving 179 people aboard. Of the estimated 179 people aboard, 76 were rescued as efforts continue to salvage the ship and recover all bodiesThe confirmed death toll from the recent capsizing of a state ferry off Guyana’s coast has risen to 72, with more bodies recovered as a multinational team struggle to salvage the partially submerged vessel. Of the estimated 179 people aboard, 76 people were rescued.

articles.title: Iran-Iraq-Pakistan ‘axis of sympathy’ signals a reshaping Southwest Asia
articles.summary: Earlier this month, the Supreme Leader of Iran, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, was buried in his hometown of Mashhad after a four-day ceremony. Many international delegations were present, but each country will have chosen their representatives with the utmost care. Sending high-ranking officials would go beyond mere diplomatic courtesy, and possibly signal an alliance. articles.title: ‘Women do not stop giving birth in an emergency’ – one month after Venezuela quakes
articles.summary: One month after twin earthquakes rocked Venezuela, thousands of women and girls continue to face difficulty in accessing essential healthcare and protection services, a senior official with the UN reproductive and sexual health agency UNFPA said on Friday. ‘Women do not stop giving birth in an emergency’ – one month after Venezuela quakes.

articles.title: After an Ebola centre was attacked, peacekeepers moved in next door
articles.summary: A new mobile UN peacekeeping base in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has allowed local authorities to continue responding to the fast-moving Ebola outbreak there after violence disrupted the work of medics at a treatment centre set up to contain the spread. After an Ebola centre was attacked, peacekeepers moved in next door.

articles.title: In El Obeid, Sudanese women face drones by day, rape by night, to reach water
articles.summary: In El Obeid, women and girls now face an impossible choice over something as basic as a bucket of water: risk a drone strike by collecting it in daylight, or risk rape by waiting until dark. In El Obeid, Sudanese women face drones by day, rape by night, to reach water.

articles.title: Masked men invading and taking Amazon communities ‘hostage’ in organised crime surge, say local
articles.summary: Delegation sent to Brasília after gunmen from organised crime group enter homes in western Amazon ForestIndigenous leaders on the Brazil-Peru border say their communities are being “taken hostage” by organised crime groups who are running rampant across the region, destroying Amazon Forest, building roads and trafficking drugs. Earlier this month, masked men armed with semi-automatic weapons entere Gangs taking villages on Brazil-Peru border ‘hostage’, say Indigenous leaders.

articles.title: Ukraine Hits More Wildberries Warehouses Near St. Petersburg, Occupied Crimea
articles.summary: Ukrainian drones struck Wildberries logistics hubs near St. Petersburg and in occupied Crimea, causing fires and disruptions. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine also hit a key military facility in Russia’s Kirov region that supplies components for aircraft and missile systems. Ukraine Hits More Wildberries Warehouses Near St. Petersburg, Occupied Crimea.

articles.title: Wildberries, 'Russia's Amazon,' Hit Again In New Wave Of Ukrainian Strikes
articles.summary: Ukraine struck targets in several parts of Russia early on July 24, including another warehouse of Russian e-commerce retailer Wildberries, as Kyiv continues to expand its retaliatory long-range strike campaign in an effort to force Moscow into negotiations. Wildberries, 'Russia's Amazon,' Hit Again In New Wave Of Ukrainian Strikes.

articles.summary: रूस और यूक्रेन ने एक-दूसरे पर हमले किए, 15 लोग मारे गए। शनिवार को रूसी कब्जे वाले जापोरिज्जिया में यूक्रेनी हमले में 12 लोगों की मौत हुई। यूक्रेन के सूमी में रूसी ड्रोन हमले में तीन लोगों की जान चली गई। Russia Ukraine Conflict: रूस और यूक्रेन के बीच जारी युद्ध एक बार फिर तेज हो गया है। शनिवार को दोनों देशों ने एक-दूसरे पर बड़े हमले किए।
